questions.prompt: An ARM template must accept only Standard_LRS or Standard_ZRS for a storageSku input. Which parameter property enforces this during validation?

options.explanation: The supplied value must be a member of this array.
A default supplies an omitted value; it does not restrict explicit input.
This documents the parameter without enforcing an allowed set.
Length validation cannot restrict the input to these two SKU names.

questions.prompt: An ARM incremental deployment redeclares an existing resource but omits one of its non-default properties. What should the administrator assume when reviewing the change?

options.text: The omitted property can reset to its default; declare the full intended configuration.
options.explanation: Incremental applies the resource definition rather than a partial property patch.

options.text: Every omitted property is preserved because the mode is incremental.
options.explanation: The preservation rule concerns omitted resources, not omitted properties on redeclared resources.

options.text: The entire resource is deleted because its definition changed.
options.explanation: Incremental does not delete the resource merely because a property is omitted.

options.text: Only the template contentVersion controls whether the property changes.
options.explanation: contentVersion is template metadata, not an update switch.

questions.prompt: An ARM template accepts an administrator password. Which TWO choices help prevent exposing it in template and deployment records?

options.explanation: Secure parameters are not stored as plain values in deployment history.

options.text: Avoid hard-coded secrets and ordinary outputs containing the password.
options.explanation: A secure input can still be exposed by how the template author uses it.

options.text: Use a string parameter with a password-like name.
options.explanation: The name does not give a regular string secure handling.

options.text: Put the password in defaultValue in the public template.
options.explanation: Secure parameter handling does not hide a literal in the source file.
